resolvedSectionBreaks.before:
When plastic deformation occurs mainly through slip, without breaking the crystal or changing its type of structure, most of the crystal can retain its ordered arrangement.
Retaining this crystalline structure does not mean that every atom keeps its original neighbors or that the lattice contains no defects, places where the pattern is imperfect.
A crystal that has undergone plastic deformation is not completely unchanged.
resolvedSectionBreaks.after:
The original textbook explains plastic deformation in terms of slip between layers of the crystal lattice.
A single crystal is one crystal, rather than many small crystals joined together.

resolvedSectionBreaks.before:
Different defects have different effects: some structures help local slip, while others obstruct dislocation motion.
The presence of defects therefore does not always make the entire crystal easier to deform plastically.
resolvedSectionBreaks.after:
A polycrystal consists of many grains, each a small crystal.
When plastic deformation occurs mainly through slip, slip can occur inside individual grains.
